chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: Andy Kirk's band, Pha Terrell and Dick Wilson
summary: He recalls Andy Kirk's organization, Mary Lou Williams, singer Pha Terrell and Dick Wilson's major-seventh sound in 1936.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah, but so many great things happened, and different guys coming through with different bands and things. And I will always remember the Andy Kirk band, because they had a great, great organization -- a great organization. They had Mary Lou Williams playing piano and writing for the band. Ben Thigpen was with the band, Ed Thigpen's father. They had Big Jim playing trumpet. They had... But the main thing was... Because also probably my favorite singer was with that band of all time -- Pha Terrell. Great singer, Pha

Terrell.
But I heard the tenor saxophone player, Dick Wilson. Fantastic tenor saxophone player. He's the first guy that I heard playing a major seventh chord. This was 1936. I heard him play that seventh chord on "Little Joe From Chicago." I said, "Wow, that note sounds strange!" And I dug around later on and found out what it was. I said, "How could get F-sharp in that G-chord," you know. But it sounded good. He put the F-sharp up there, you know, heh-heh...
